chapter: Other New Orleans clubs and bands
title: Sam Morgan's band and the Hummingbird
summary: He plays a year with Sam Morgan's band and fills in for George Guesnon at the Hummingbird club.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, my wife, my wife could tell you right now her address. We'll get it done after a while. Yeah. Well, anyway, after I left, after I left, after I left, I went to, uh, Sam Morgan's band. But I was just working in somebody else's place. I wasn't supposed to be in my place, but I played with his band one year. Sam Morgan's. You see. I played one night club called, they call it the Humming Boys. Oh yeah. George Gaynor told me about that place. Well, I, I, I take George's place in there. George, uh, uh, uh, got shot in the leg accidentally, you see. And they put me in here. I played, went and played in his place for a while. See, but I left from there. That's the place George Gaynor was playing in. And when in another place, the same people open up, call it, and they call it the Humming Boys. Now, we, uh, in that plane, we had a boy named Henry Jury and played saxophone and the same guy was playing drum then, played drums. That's right. And, and, uh, uh, what you call them, uh, uh, Joe Robichaux was playing piano, you see. And, uh, the trumpet player, let's see, who was the trumpet player? I don't know if it was, I don't know if it was. That's right, somebody else can tell us. Well, after Henry Julian left, we had, uh, uh, Colbert, Jim Colbert playing saxophone, and, and, uh, Albert de Conje playing trumpet. And the, and the rest of the fellas, you know, I gave cards to myself. I was playing banjoling, you see. And I left from there and went on the music box playing the banjol. You heard of the music box?
